title: Live-cell imaging protocol for organelle morphology analysis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
author: Deolal, Mishra
materials: Yeast Nitrogen Base without amino acids

steps.title: Prepare SC dropout powder mix
steps.instruction: Combine the following reagents in a blender (or mortar and pestle) to make 100 mL of SC dropout medium: Yeast Nitrogen Base without amino acids (1×, 50 g L⁻¹), Arginine Sulfate (20 mg L⁻¹, 150 mg L⁻¹), Glutamic Acid (100 mg L⁻¹, 3.75 g L⁻¹), Histidine HCl (20 mg L⁻¹, 150 mg L⁻¹), Isoleucine (30 mg L⁻¹, 225 mg L⁻¹), Leucine HCl (100 mg L⁻¹, 450 mg L⁻¹), Methionine (20 mg L⁻¹, 150 mg L⁻¹), Phenylalanine (50 mg L⁻¹, 435 mg L⁻¹), Tryptophan (20 mg L⁻¹, 150 mg L⁻¹), Tyrosine (30 mg L⁻¹, 225 mg L⁻¹), Valine (150 mg L⁻¹, 1.12 g L⁻¹), Adenine Sulfate (20 mg L⁻¹, 150 mg L⁻¹), Uracil (20 mg L⁻¹, 150 mg L⁻¹). Store the powder at 22 °C–26 °C for up to 1 year. Ready‑made dropout mix may be purchased as an alternative.

steps.title: Prepare complete SC growth medium
steps.instruction: To the powder mix add dextrose to 2 % (2 g L⁻¹) and, for plates, agar to 2 % (2 g L⁻¹). Adjust the pH to 5.8–6.2 with drops of 10 N NaOH. Autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min. Store the sterilized medium at 22 °C–26 °C for up to 6 months. Use the synthetic complete (SC) formulation for imaging because of its low autofluorescence.

steps.title: Grow yeast starter culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate a single colony into appropriate synthetic minimal or complete SC medium and incubate overnight (12–14 h) at 30 °C with shaking at 220 rpm. The next day sub‑culture into fresh medium to an initial OD₆₀₀ of 0.15–0.2 and grow for 3–4 h at 30 °C, 220 rpm.

steps.title: Harvest mid‑log cells
steps.instruction: Collect cells when the culture reaches OD₆₀₀ 0.6–1.0. Spin 1 mL of culture at 3000 g for 1 min. Wash the pellet with 1 mL of fresh SC medium pre‑warmed to 30 °C. Resuspend the washed pellet in 20–50 µL of SC medium.

steps.title: Coat glass‑bottom dish with ConA
steps.instruction: Apply 0.1 % (w/v) concanavalin A (ConA) to the glass surface. For a 25 mm diameter dish, spread 20 µL of the 0.1 % ConA solution and let it bind (no incubation time specified).

steps.title: Immobilize cells for imaging
steps.instruction: Place 10 µL of the cell suspension onto the ConA‑coated dish and spread gently with a P200 pipette tip. Allow cells to adhere undisturbed for 3–5 min. Add 500 µL of SC medium, mix up‑and‑down gently (do not pipette directly over the cells), then remove the liquid. Repeat the add‑mix‑remove step two more times. Finally add 500 µL–1 mL fresh SC medium and begin imaging. This yields ~35–50 cells per 50 µm × 50 µm field; cells remain healthy for up to 12 h in 2 % glucose. Adjust cell density by varying the volume of cell suspension applied.

steps.title: Acquire live‑cell images
steps.instruction: Place the dish on a temperature‑controlled stage (typically 30 °C) and record time‑lapse images as required. Cells can be imaged for up to 12 h without loss of viability.

steps.title: Deconvolve images with Huygens
steps.instruction: Export the acquired image files to Huygens Professional v17.04. Verify Nyquist sampling parameters in the thumbnail view; if parameters are sub‑optimal, acquire new images. Right‑click the image, select ‘Deconvolution Wizard’, and let the software estimate background (in/near object mode). Use the GMLE (Good’s roughness Maximum Likelihood Estimation) algorithm, set the signal‑to‑noise ratio (SNR) between 10 and 14 (example SNR 12), and run the default number of iterations. The software will generate deconvolved images based on a theoretically computed PSF.

steps.title: Measure nuclear circularity in FIJI
steps.instruction: Open the deconvolved image in FIJI. Choose Analyze → Set Measurements and enable ‘Shape descriptors’ (and any other desired parameters). Using the Freehand selection tool, trace the outline of each nucleus (avoid dividing cells, nuclei not fully captured, and edge cells). Adjust the line width via Edit → Options if needed. After each trace, press T or use Edit → Selection → Add to Manager to store the ROI; ensure the ‘Label’ box is checked to avoid duplicates. Once all nuclei are marked, click Measure; the Results window will list area, perimeter, circularity (4 π × area / perimeter²), etc. Export the table as .csv or copy to Excel.

steps.title: Optional: Analyze ER morphology
steps.instruction: In FIJI, similarly trace the perinuclear ER (pER) and cortical ER (cER) using the Freehand tool, then use the Line tool to draw a line across the cell. Choose Analyze → Plot Profile to obtain fluorescence intensity along the line. Export the intensity data as .csv. Compute an aggregation index or other intensity‑variation metrics as desired. Perform this for at least 10–15 cells from three independent experiments.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of circularity
steps.instruction: Collect measurements from at least 30 cells per biological replicate (3 replicates total, ≥90 cells). Use Student’s t‑test to compare the circularity index between experimental strains (e.g., wild type vs. ssf1Δ), assuming random sampling and normal distribution of the data.
